title: Returning a Headset
instructions: Listen carefully. Choose the option that best matches what is said or implied.

audio.description: A customer asks about returning an unused item after its packaging was opened.

transcript.text: I bought this headset ten days ago. The microphone sounds poor on my laptop. The box is open, but I have all parts and the receipt. Can I return it?
We should test it first; this may be a laptop setting. If faulty, we can exchange or refund it. Returns within thirty days also require complete packaging.
It did the same on another computer, so it seems faulty.
I can check it now. If another is in stock, would you prefer an exchange or a refund?
A refund, please. I can borrow one this week and compare a few models before buying again.

questions.prompt: What problem does the customer report?
options: The headset cannot connect to the internet.
Several parts are missing from the box.
The headset microphone works poorly with their laptop.
The receipt shows the wrong price.
questions.explanation: The customer says the microphone does not work well with the laptop.

questions.prompt: Why will the assistant test the headset first?
options: The problem could be caused by a laptop setting.
questions.explanation: The assistant says the issue might be a laptop setting, so they will test the headset.

questions.prompt: What does the customer say supports their view that the headset is faulty?
options: It had the same problem on another computer.
They have used it for thirty days.
The box was damaged before purchase.
The assistant tested it last week.
questions.explanation: The customer says they tried it on another computer and experienced the same issue.

questions.prompt: Why does the customer choose a refund?
options: They prefer the packaging of another one.
They have already bought an identical headset.
They want time to compare other models.
questions.explanation: They can borrow one for the week and want to compare models before buying again.
